title: Migration reconciliation and approval-bound cutover
summary: A realistic synthetic process-local conformance model reconciles immutable migration generations and atomically publishes active, prior, approval-consumption, receipt, and event state for one exactly bound cutover request.

failureModes: A candidate generation identity can arrive with changed canonical content.
Active and candidate generations can contain missing, divergent, or extra identities, or supplied restore evidence can remain incomplete.
Current state, request meaning, approval identity, approval scope, or approval time can differ from the prepared plan.
Activation publication can stop before the state swap or its response can be lost after publication.
recoveryMoves: Preserve the accepted generation and issue a distinct candidate identity for changed content.
Return the complete reconciliation or restore route while the accepted generation remains available.
Return the typed changed fields or reason and form a current request or approval from an eligible approver distinct from the actor when appropriate.
Retry from the accepted snapshot after a pre-publication interruption, or replay the recorded receipt with the exact original request-and-approval pair after post-publication response loss.
